record_type_quote: This multicenter replication study aimed to validate the findings and evaluate the oncologic impacts of e-cigarette use during chemotherapy.

targets.authors: Manyanga J, Ganapathy V, Bouharati C, Mehta T, Sadhasivam B, Acharya P, et al.
targets.title: Electronic cigarette aerosols alter the expression of cisplatin transporters and increase drug resistance in oral cancer cells
targets.evidence_quote: This collaborative replication study aimed to verify findings from Manyanga et al. under harmonized and standardized conditions, addressing previously reported limitations such as non-standardized exposure systems, to enhance data reproducibility and comparability [16–18].
targets.outcome_quote: Although our study did not replicate the increase in cisplatin resistance observed in previous studies, it contributes valuable data to the ongoing debate about the nicotine use and cancer therapy, suggesting that more comprehensive investigations are needed to better understand these effects and their clinical implications.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall conclusion explicitly says the cisplatin resistance increase did not replicate. Some gene-expression comparisons agree, but this does not override the overall verdict on the central finding.

reasoning: New multicenter cell experiments explicitly retest Manyanga et al. (2021). Other cited studies motivate the work rather than being independently identified targets. Title, DOI and author list match.
